seo.metaTitle: Create Empty PNG - Blank Image Generator, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Create a blank PNG of any size in your browser: fully transparent or filled with a solid color. No signup, no limits, generated and downloaded instantly.
seo.longDescription: Creating an empty PNG gives you a blank canvas of exactly the size you ask for, either fully transparent or filled with one solid color. Nothing is uploaded because there is nothing to upload: the canvas is generated on your device from the width, height, opacity and color you set, and the file is encoded and saved straight to your machine. Use it as a backdrop for a mockup, as a transparent layer in a design tool, as a spacer in a layout, or as a placeholder that has the exact dimensions your project expects. Sizes run from 1 to 20000 pixels on each side, with presets for the common formats.
howTo: Set Width and Height in pixels, or pick one of the presets such as a square or a screen size.
Leave Opacity at 0 for a fully transparent canvas, or raise it to fill with the chosen color.
Pick the fill color if you want a solid background instead of transparency.
Download the generated PNG from the Download button.

faq.q: How do I make a transparent PNG?
faq.a: Set Opacity to 0. Every pixel is then written with a fully transparent alpha channel, which is exactly what a transparent PNG is. Raising the slider fills the canvas with the fill color instead; partial values give a semi-transparent sheet.

faq.q: What size can the canvas be?
faq.a: From 1 to 20000 pixels per side, with presets for the usual targets. Very large canvases take a moment to generate because every pixel is filled - a 20000 by 20000 canvas is 400 million pixels.

faq.q: Is the file really a valid PNG?
faq.a: Yes. The canvas is encoded as a real PNG by the browser, not a renamed blank file, so it opens in any image viewer and works as a source image for the other tools on this site.

faq.q: Do I have to sign up or upload anything?
faq.a: No account, no upload, no daily limit, no watermark. The canvas is created and encoded in your browser, and the tool is free for commercial use and open source.
